criteria.criterion: A new gate test squash-merges a verified landing onto main as one commit whose message has no Athena-* trailers; `cargo test -p athena-gate` shows the history check and invariant report no violations for it.
criteria.evidence: landing_tests::a_squash_merge_with_no_trailers_lands commits code and all job records with the message "Change a (#1)\n" and asserts that both invariant::check and history::check_history return no violations. The test passed.

criteria.criterion: A new gate test rebase-merges a verified landing (new commit ids, prediction commit not an ancestor by id); `cargo test -p athena-gate` shows it passes.
criteria.evidence: a_rebase_merge_lands_though_the_prediction_commit_is_no_ancestor moves main forward, cherry-picks the PR commits onto it and fast-forwards. It asserts !is_ancestor(prediction, main) and that the history walk finds no violations. The test passed.

criteria.criterion: A new test shows a squash commit that changes governed content without the job's valid records is refused with Rule::Invariant; `cargo test -p athena-gate` passes.
criteria.evidence: a_squash_that_changes_governed_content_without_the_jobs_records_is_refused covers two cases: a commit with no records, and a commit whose records verify a different fingerprint. Each produces exactly one Rule::Invariant violation. The test passed.

criteria.criterion: A new test shows a squashed landing whose records show the reading was written after the work (prediction not before the invocations) is refused; `cargo test -p athena-gate` passes.
criteria.evidence: a_squash_whose_reading_was_written_after_the_work_is_refused covers two cases: a reading after dispatched_at, and, with no dispatch time, a reading after the producer started. Each is refused with Rule::Invariant, and the history walk also reports a violation. The test passed.

criteria.criterion: A new test shows a second landing of the same job after a squash is refused, and an edited or conflicting trailer on a squash does not make an otherwise valid landing pass or fail wrongly; `cargo test -p athena-gate` passes.
criteria.evidence: a_second_landing_of_the_same_job_after_a_squash_is_refused asserts that the history walk reports 'already landed' on the second squash. trailers_on_a_squash_neither_admit_nor_refuse_by_themselves checks three things: agreeing or stale trailers (including a bogus Athena-Prediction) change nothing; a conflicting Athena-Job or Athena-Verified-Content is refused; and trailers alone cannot admit a change that has no records. Both tests passed.

criteria.criterion: Existing merge-commit tests still pass: `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo fmt --check` are all clean.
criteria.evidence: Every test binary reported 'ok' with 0 failures. Clippy and fmt both finished with no output.

criteria.criterion: docs/design/athena-v0.md §7.3/§7.4 describes how the invariant treats merge, squash and rebase merges, that trailers are not relied on, how prediction-before-work is proved from records, and the alternatives considered, citing the code.
criteria.evidence: §7.3 gains these parts: 'Merge, squash, and rebase merges' (citing `landing` and `closing_jobs` in invariant.rs), 'Trailers are hints, not evidence', 'Prediction before work, from the records' (citing `prediction_problem`, and stating the limits of the proof), 'No second landing' (citing `HistoryState::landed`), and five alternatives considered. In §7.4, item 7 is updated.

criteria.criterion: The module doc of crates/athena-gate/src/invariant.rs matches the new rules.
criteria.evidence: The module doc's case (a) is rewritten: the job is identified from the closing records, trailers and ancestry are not used, prediction order comes from the reading's time and invocation number, the no-second-landing rule checks the parent's records plus the history walk, and conflicting trailers are refused. This matches the `landing` and `prediction_problem` code.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry, and README.md says merge, squash and rebase merges are all supported.
criteria.evidence: CHANGELOG has a new Unreleased 'Changed' entry. README has a new 'Merge strategy' paragraph saying merge commit, squash merge and rebase merge are all accepted.

findings.summary: Design §8 M23 row and the §7.3 trailer description still describe the old ancestry-based Athena-Prediction check
findings.evidence: Line 1134 still reads 'the `Athena-Prediction` trailer and its CI check … a closing commit whose prediction commit is not an ancestor'. Line 912 still says '`Athena-Prediction` names the commit that proves the forecast came first'. Both contradict the new §7.3 text and docs/enforcement.md, which were updated.

findings.summary: Rule::Prediction is now never reported but remains in the enum
findings.evidence: check_prediction was removed, and grep finds no remaining constructor of Rule::Prediction. The CHANGELOG says the rule 'no longer reports', but the variant and its description are still there.

findings.summary: A squash that carries closing records for two jobs (e.g. an abandoned job's outcome.json alongside the landed one) is refused
findings.evidence: closing_jobs counts any added outcome.json, whatever its state, and landing refuses with 'a commit adds closing records for more than one job'. A PR that squashes an abandoned job together with a landed one would therefore fail. The docs do not mention this limit.

summary: The change does what you asked: Athena now accepts pull requests landed by squash merge and rebase merge, as well as by merge commit. It meets all 9 acceptance criteria, so the verdict is pass. The gate no longer uses commit trailers or commit ancestry to recognise a landing. It finds the job from the records the commit adds, and proves the reading came before the work from the times and order those records hold. A trailer that contradicts the records still refuses the landing. A job landing twice is caught by the parent commit's records and by the history walk. Six new tests cover squash, rebase, missing records, a reading written after the work, a second landing, and edited or conflicting trailers. I ran them and all passed, and the full `cargo test`, clippy and fmt runs were clean. The design doc §7.3/§7.4, the module doc, CHANGELOG, README, records.md and enforcement.md were updated. Three minor issues remain: (1) two places in the design doc (§8's M23 row and the landing-trailer description) still describe the old ancestry check; (2) `Rule::Prediction` is no longer reported by anything but still exists in the code; (3) a squash that closes two jobs in one commit, such as an abandoned job alongside the landed one, is refused, and the docs don't mention this.
